Q: Problem compiling a skeleton CUDA & C++ project using CMake A:

Basically, you're mixing up files which should be compiled with a regular C++ compiler and files which need to be compiled with a CUDA-enabled compiler; and I am making the educated guess that your files don't contain exactly what you said they contain.

Let's start with the error you're getting though. Your compiler says it can't find crt/host_runtime.h. Ok, what's that? Well, it's a CUDA-related include and part of the CUDA distribution. So if you installed CUDA at, say, /usr/local/cuda, it would be at: /usr/local/cuda/include/crt/host_runtime.h.

That means one of two things is wrong: Either you should have somehow had that include directory on the list of include dirs the compiler is aware of, or you did something which triggered a dependence on that file despite not including it directly.

The former is not true - since we're talking about a .cpp file which CMake (rightly) compiles with your host-side-code C++ compiler. Such code would not include that file.

It is likely the latter. I'm guessing that something in your main.cpp, host.h or device.cuh does try to do something a kernel launch, or has other CUDA-ish device-side definitions etc, triggering the requirement of the header.

Other notes:

  1. c++ as the C++ compiler is typically an alias, implemented via a symlink. You can check this pretty easily. On my system:

    $ readlink  /usr/bin/c++
g++-7

  2. You should not hard-code compiler locations and compute architecture numbers into your CMakeLists.txt. The idea is for that file to be valid regardless of where you build the project, regardless of the GPU you have on your system at a given time and perhaps even of your OS. Because - the project code doesn't really depend on any of those. When you call CMake, it will either detect them, or you can use the command-line, and/or the environment, and/or a toolchain file, to tell CMake about what it needs to know.

Q: How to avoid the partial function Map.lookup, when the key is known to be in the map? A:

How about handling all the duplicates at once?

replace :: [(Char, Int)] -> [(Char, Foo)]
replace [] = []
replace x@((c, i):cis) = [(c', replacement) | (c', _) <- sameI] ++ replace diffI
    where
    (sameI, diffI) = partition (\(_, i') -> i == i') x
    replacement = Foo . sum . map snd $ cis

This will compute different replacements than yours with the sum way of choosing a replacement, but perhaps in your situation the choice is more robust to deleting subcomponents in the recursive step.

> replace [('a',3), ('c',20), ('d',7), ('d',3), ('a',20)]
[('a',Foo 50),('d',Foo 50),('c',Foo 27),('a',Foo 27),('d',Foo 0)]
-- ('a',3)    ('d',3)      ('c',20)     ('a',20)     ('d',7)

Unfortunately this way, though concise, has worse asymptotics.* This can be fixed by splitting into three lists instead of just two and binary searching. I didn't start with that because it's enough more complicated that I think it's hiding the key idea. But here's how that would look:

splitOn :: Ord b => (a -> b) -> b -> [a] -> ([a], [a], [a])
splitOn f pivot = go where
    go [] = ([], [], [])
    go (a:as) = let (lt, eq, gt) = go as in case compare (f a) pivot of
        LT -> (a:lt, eq, gt)
        EQ -> (lt, a:eq, gt)
        GT -> (lt, eq, a:gt)

replace :: [(Char, Int)] -> [(Char, Foo)]
replace [] = []
replace other = go (minimum (snd <$> other)) (maximum (snd <$> other)) other where
    go lo hi [] = []
    go lo hi cis = result where
        med = (lo + hi) `div` 2
        (lt, eq, gt) = splitOn snd med cis
        replacement = Foo . sum . map snd $ cis
        result = []
            ++ go lo (med-1) lt
            ++ [(c', replacement) | (c', _) <- eq]
            ++ go (med+1) hi gt

* Well, it would have worse asymptotics if you were using a more efficient function than sum to choose the replacement values. All the Map stuff together is O(n*log(n)), but the repeated calls to sum make it O(n2). The naive first version of the function in this answer is also O(n2), but it is fundamentally so, even if you replace sum with something else.

Q: htaccess for clean URLs and redirecting A:

I am using .htacess to convert URLs with php variables to clean URLs.

To clarify, you don't "use .htaccess to convert URLs with php variables to clean URLs" (and that is not what you are doing here). It's the other way round. You use .htaccess to internally rewrite ("convert") clean URLs into URLs with "PHP variables" for PHP to then process. And, strictly speaking, these are "URL parameters", not "PHP variables" (the "PHP variables" come later when PHP converts/decodes the URL parameters to be easily accessible from PHP).

You can also (optionally) redirect URLs with URL parameters to "clean URLs". This is the bit you are stuck on.

RewriteRule ^productgroup/([0-9a-zA-Z]+)$ products/index.php?Cid=$1 [NC,L]

This rule is already complete. If you add an R (redirect) flag to this rule then you are changing it from an internal rewrite into an external redirect. And you are redirecting in the wrong direction (from the "clean URL" to the "URL params").

However, I would question whether you should be using the NC (nocase) flag here, as this potentially opens the site up to duplicate content issues. (ie. Why do you need to allow both productgroup and PRODUCTGROUP and every variation inbetween? These are technically different URLs and consequently are treated differently by search engines.) At the very least, you are unnecessarily rewritting URLs you are not interested in and forcing PHP to process them.

Also, do you need/want to allow uppercase letters (A-Z) in the 2nd path segment? (Do you have mixed case URLs?)

In order to externally redirect requests from products/index.php?Cid=<value> to productgroup/<value> you need to add an additional rule before the above rewrite.

For example, to redirect from /products/index.php?Cid=<value> to /productgroup/<value>:

RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} ^Cid=([0-9a-zA-Z]+)$
RewriteRule ^products/index\.php$ /productgroup/%1 [QSD,R=301,L]

The RewriteRule pattern only matches against the URL-path (not the query string), hence the need for an additional condition (RewriteCond directive) to match (and capture) the query string.

The %1 backreference contains the value of the Cid URL parameter as captured in the preceding condition (RewriteCond directive). But note the A-Z in the regex, as mentioned above (is this rquired?).

UPDATE: The QSD (Query String Discard) flag (Apache 2.4) is necessary to remove the original query string from the redirect response.

You will also need to change your exitsing rule (the "internal rewrite") to use the END flag (Apache 2.4) instead of L in order to avoid a redirect loop. (Or, you can check the REDIRECT_STATUS environment variable in the above/redirect rule to make sure you are only checking direct requests and not internally rewritten requests by the later rewrite. This would be required if you are on Apache 2.2 for instance.) If you are on LiteSpeed (an Apache replacement) then it doesn't matter as L and END are effectively the same.

Note that this should be a 301 (permanent) redirect. However, test first with a 302 (temporary) redirect to avoid potential caching issues.

Your complete .htaccess would then become:

RewriteEngine On

# Externally redirect "/products/index.php?Cid=<value>" to "/productgroup/<value>"
RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} ^Cid=([0-9a-zA-Z]+)$
RewriteRule ^products/index\.php$ /productgroup/%1 [QSD,R=301,L]

# Internally rewrite "/productgroup/<value>" to "/products/index.php?Cid=<value>"
RewriteRule ^productgroup/([0-9a-zA-Z]+)$ products/index.php?Cid=$1 [END]

The RewriteBase directive is not required here.

This assumes you are internally linking to the "clean URLs" throughout your HTML.

Q: .gitignore syntax - how to exclude virtualenv sub-directories? A:

When you create some venv like python -m venv sampleenv, a folder named "sampleenv" is created for you with some files and folders in it. One of those files is .gitignore file containing one line: *. Which means you don't have to do any other thing to exclude venv folders because they are already excluded.
